## Concepts

### Power as the rate of energy transfer

`phy.energy.power` · AQA 4.1.1.4 · tier Both

**Objective.** Define power as the rate of energy transfer or of doing work, recall P = E/t and P = W/t, and explain examples (two motors lifting the same load at different rates).

**Prerequisites.** Substituting into and rearranging equations (hard); Units, prefixes and conversions (hard).

**Secure evidence must cover.** calculation; comparison-explanation; includes a typed numeric answer.

**Out of scope here.** Electrical power (P = VI, P = I²R) belongs to Electricity.

| Misconception | The correct idea | What it looks like | If you see it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MIS-PHY-ENE-011` Confuses power with energy: a more powerful device must transfer more energy, regardless of time. | Power is the rate of transfer. A more powerful device transfers the same energy in less time. | says the faster motor transfers more energy lifting the same load the same height | Misconception clinic. name the misconception and why it is tempting → contrasting cases (right idea vs the misconception) → targeted micro-practice (3 items) → second mastery check on different questions. |

### Dissipation, reducing unwanted transfers and efficiency

`phy.energy.dissipation-efficiency` · AQA 4.1.2.1; AQA 4.1.2.2 · tier Both

**Objective.** Explain dissipation and ways of reducing unwanted transfers (lubrication, thermal insulation, wall thickness and thermal conductivity), and recall and use both efficiency equations as a decimal or a percentage.

**Prerequisites.** Conservation of energy in a closed system (hard); Substituting into and rearranging equations (soft).

**Secure evidence must cover.** efficiency-calculation; reducing-transfers; includes a typed numeric answer.

**Out of scope here.** No definition of thermal conductivity; Required practical 2 (thermal insulators) is separate-only: tag such items separateOnly.

| Misconception | The correct idea | What it looks like | If you see it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MIS-PHY-ENE-003` Friction or air resistance destroys energy (so the "missing" energy has vanished). | Work done against friction transfers energy to the thermal store of the object and surroundings; it is dissipated, not destroyed. | chooses "destroyed by friction" | Misconception clinic. name the misconception and why it is tempting → contrasting cases (right idea vs the misconception) → targeted micro-practice (3 items) → second mastery check on different questions. |
| `MIS-PHY-ENE-012` Inverts the efficiency ratio (total ÷ useful), giving a value above 1, or gives efficiency a unit. | efficiency = useful output ÷ total input, always ≤ 1 (≤ 100%), with no unit. | efficiency > 1; efficiency given in J or W | Worked-example re-teach. alternative explanation → scaffolded worked example, then a faded one → targeted micro-practice (3 items) → second mastery check on different questions. |
| `MIS-PHY-ENE-018` Thinks lubrication adds energy to a machine, rather than reducing the energy dissipated by friction. | A lubricant reduces friction, so less energy is dissipated to thermal stores; it supplies no energy. | chooses "the oil gives the machine energy" | Misconception clinic. name the misconception and why it is tempting → contrasting cases (right idea vs the misconception) → targeted micro-practice (3 items) → second mastery check on different questions. |
| `MIS-PHY-ENE-019` Thinks energy dissipated to the surroundings can easily be recovered and used. | Dissipated energy is spread out in the thermal store of the surroundings and becomes less useful; in practice it cannot be recovered. | chooses "the wasted energy can be collected and reused" | Misconception clinic. name the misconception and why it is tempting → contrasting cases (right idea vs the misconception) → targeted micro-practice (3 items) → second mastery check on different questions. |

### National and global energy resources

`phy.energy.resources` · AQA 4.1.3 · tier Both

**Objective.** Describe the main energy resources and their uses, distinguish renewable from non-renewable, compare reliability and environmental impact, explain trends, and evaluate why science alone cannot always resolve the issues.

**Prerequisites.** none.

**Secure evidence must cover.** classification; evaluation.

**Out of scope here.** How resources generate electricity is not required.

| Misconception | The correct idea | What it looks like | If you see it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MIS-PHY-ENE-013` Equates renewable with "no environmental impact" or "always reliable". | Renewable means it is (or can be) replenished as it is used. Many renewables have environmental impacts and several (wind, solar, waves) are not always available. | chooses renewable as "does not harm the environment" | Misconception clinic. name the misconception and why it is tempting → contrasting cases (right idea vs the misconception) → targeted micro-practice (3 items) → second mastery check on different questions. |
| `MIS-PHY-ENE-017` Classes nuclear fuel as renewable (because it is low-carbon or lasts a long time). | Nuclear fuel (uranium, plutonium) is not replenished as it is used, so it is non-renewable, even though it produces little carbon dioxide. | chooses nuclear as renewable | Misconception clinic. name the misconception and why it is tempting → contrasting cases (right idea vs the misconception) → targeted micro-practice (3 items) → second mastery check on different questions. |

## Hinge questions (ask, then decide whether to move on)

1. **Motor A lifts a load through 2 m in 4 s. Motor B lifts the same load through 2 m in 8 s. Which motor has the greater power, and why?**
   - Answer: Motor A: both do the same work (transfer the same energy), and A does it in less time.
   - Wrong answers usually mean: `MIS-PHY-ENE-011` Confuses power with energy: a more powerful device must transfer more energy, regardless of time.

2. **A motor is supplied with 500 J and transfers 350 J usefully. What is its efficiency?**
   - Answer: 350 ÷ 500 = 0.70 (70%). No unit, and never more than 1.
   - Wrong answers usually mean: `MIS-PHY-ENE-012` Inverts the efficiency ratio (total ÷ useful), giving a value above 1, or gives efficiency a unit.

3. **Why is wind a less reliable resource than gas for generating electricity?**
   - Answer: Wind turbines only generate when the wind is blowing, and output varies with wind speed; gas can be burned whenever electricity is needed.
   - Wrong answers usually mean: `MIS-PHY-ENE-013` Equates renewable with "no environmental impact" or "always reliable".

## Stretch

A 1.2 kW kettle takes 3.0 minutes to heat water. The water gains 180 kJ. Calculate the efficiency of the kettle. Answer: E supplied = 1200 × 180 = 216 000 J; efficiency = 180 000 ÷ 216 000 = 0.83 (83%).

A concept is **Secure** when all of these hold (mastery-rules-v1.0):

- at least 4 of the pupil's last 5 answers on it are right, across at least 3 different questions;
- right answers in at least 2 sessions at least 24 hours apart;
- at least one right typed (numeric) or written answer, where the concept is a calculation;
- at least one right answer at difficulty band 2 or above;
- at least one right **mastery-check** question (the diagnostic alone can never make a concept secure);
- no likely misconception still open, and every required context covered.

Guards: an MCQ answered right but "unsure" counts half; the same question again within 14 days does not count again. **Mastered** also needs a right retrieval answer at least 21 days after becoming secure, and a right exam-style application question where the concept needs one. In a 6-week programme, expect Secure, not Mastered.

## Notes for the teacher

- Power is a rate: always ask "in how long?" when a pupil compares devices by energy alone.
- Resources: assess evaluation (reliability, environmental impact, cost) as well as classification. Nuclear is non-renewable.
